question.text: What will be the total retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood in 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the estimated retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood during 2026, according to the [Good Food Institute](https://gfi.org/resource/state-of-the-industry-downloads/)'s 2027 State of the Industry reports.
question.fine_print:
If the Good Food Institute changes their reporting structure, this question will resolve based upon their first official estimate for the year 2026 made during 2027.

If the Good Food Institute does not release a relevant report before 2028 this question will be annulled.

research:
I'm wrapping up the research now and writing the brief.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-04 (2026 State of the Industry report): GFI, using Euromonitor data, puts **global** retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood at **$6.6B in 2025**. That is +8% in nominal terms, about +4% after inflation, and about +3% in volume. It was ~$2.2B in 2015. I could not fetch the full PDF (too large), so these figures come from the GFI summary and press coverage. [GFI summary](https://gfi.org/pb-summary-2026), [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/gfi-state-of-the-industry-report-2025-2026-plant-based-sales/)
- Note that this series is global (Euromonitor), in nominal USD. It is not the US SPINS series. GFI's US plant-based meat and seafood figure was ~$1.0B in 2025, down 10% in dollars and 11% in units. [Dairy Processing](https://www.dairyprocessing.com/articles/4149-us-plant-based-sales-continue-to-decline), [Food Business News](https://www.foodbusinessnews.net/articles/30327-plant-based-sales-in-the-us-continue-to-slide)
- The 2027 report, which will cover 2026, should come out around April 2027, going by past timing.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. No 2026 global estimate exists. The Euromonitor/GFI figure comes out only in the annual report.
- Earlier years' figures get revised between editions. The 2024 report gave 2023 as $6.4B. The 2025 report then gave 2024 as $6.1B, "up 4%", which implies 2023 was revised down to about $5.9B. So the 2025 baseline of $6.6B could itself be restated in the 2027 report. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-meat-by-numbers-grim-reading-for-the-us-retail-market-brighter-spots-in-foodservice-and-glo), [GFI 2024 summary](https://gfi.org/2024-plant-based-state-of-the-industry-summary-pdf)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Beyond Meat Q3 2026 net revenue was $64.5M, down 8% year on year and at the top of its $60-65M guidance. Gross margin was 19.3%. I could not confirm a channel breakdown. [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/11/62900633/beyond-meat-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript)
- 2026-11-03: A Madre Brava/Systemiq report argues German retailers could set off a plant-based tipping point by 2030. [vegconomist](https://vegconomist.com/retail-e-commerce/tipping-point-possible-2030-madre-brava-sees-food-retail-sector-catalyst-protein-transition/)
- 2026-08 (Q2 10-Q): Beyond Meat Q2 2026 US retail was $29.6M (-9.9%), international retail $18.5M (+16.5%), and total revenue $68.8M (-8.2%). [SEC 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001655210/000165521026000055/bynd-20260627.htm), [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/beyond-meat-earnings-q2-2026-sales-revenue-immerse-protein-drink-europe/)
- 2026-07: Lebensmittel Zeitung, as cited by Bryant Research, reports German plant-based meat volumes up 17% in early 2026 versus the same period of 2025. This is secondhand and I did not verify it. [Bryant Research](https://bryantresearch.co.uk/insight-items/the-great-plant-based-comeback/)
- 2026-06: GFI Europe reports French plant-based meat volumes up 17% in 2025. [Bryant Research](https://bryantresearch.co.uk/insight-items/the-great-plant-based-comeback/)
- 2026-04-21: GFI says the 2025 growth came largely from Europe, which offset US declines. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/gfi-state-of-the-industry-report-2025-2026-plant-based-sales/)
- I found no Circana or SPINS totals for the US in 2026.
- Currency: the figure is in nominal USD, so exchange rates matter. EUR/USD peaked at ~1.20-1.21 in late January 2026 and fell to ~1.12 by late October 2026. Sources conflict, so check ECB rates. If the year averages above 2025's level (my unverified recollection is ~1.13), European sales convert to more dollars, though the boost would be modest. [Pound Sterling Live](https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/EUR-USD-2026)

## 4. Base rates
- Figures as first published by GFI:
  - 2015: $2.2B
  - 2023: $6.4B (2024 report)
  - 2024: $6.1B, +4% (2025 report)
  - 2025: $6.6B, +8% (2026 report)
- Recent nominal growth has run about 4-8% a year. Applied to $6.6B, that gives roughly $6.85-7.1B, but this is arithmetic, not a forecast.
- Revisions between editions have been about ±5%, as large as a year's growth. This is the main source of uncertainty: in the 2025 report, the 2024 figure came in below the 2023 figure published the year before.
- Inflation added about 4 points to 2025's nominal growth.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. The Kalshi markets supplied with the brief (UK/US retail sales, Loblaw, broilers, and others) do not match it.
- Commercial market-research forecasts, such as ResearchAndMarkets' plant-based food market at $34.29B in 2026 with a 10.6% annual growth rate, use different scopes and are not comparable to the Euromonitor/GFI series. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/04/3395399/28124/en/plant-based-food-market-size-share-trends-global-forecast-to-2036-market-to-reach-93-95-billion-at-10-6-cagr-driven-by-flexitarian-demand-and-asia-pacific-expansion-beyond-meat-imp.html)
- I found no expert forecast of GFI's 2026 number.

## 6. Upcoming events
- Late 2026 or early 2027: full-year SPINS/Circana US data and European retail panels (Germany, UK, France).
- Early 2027: Beyond Meat Q4 and full-year 2026 results, with a split between US and international retail.
- Year-end 2026: final EUR/USD and other currency averages.
- About April 2027: GFI's 2027 State of the Industry reports, the resolution source, including any Euromonitor restatement of the 2025 baseline.

Other sources: [vegconomist GFI 2026 coverage](https://vegconomist.com/studies-numbers/gfis-2026-state-of-industry-reports-detail-mixed-year-alternative-proteins-across-three-sectors), [Frozen Food Europe](https://www.frozenfoodeurope.com/alternative-protein-sector-shows-signs-of-recovery-despite-uneven-consumer-demand/), [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/04/21/plant-based-meat-only-4-of-plant-based-market/)

  - 2023: $6.4B (first estimate)

- The question says sales were $2.2B in 2015. That number probably comes from a different series, not this Euromonitor one, so the long-run trend may not compare directly.
- The US makes up a small and shrinking share (about $1B, falling roughly 10% a year). Europe (about $3.6B) and Asia-Pacific drive the global total. A weaker US dollar in 2026 would push up euro-denominated sales when converted to dollars. I did not check 2026 exchange rates.

- Commercial market-research forecasts, such as ResearchAndMarkets' $34.29B for global plant-based food in 2026, use different definitions and don't map onto GFI/Euromonitor. forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The GFI 2027 State of the Industry report, which settles the question, should come out around April 2027. That is about 5 months away, and about 2 months after forecasts close.

(b) The latest value is $6.6B global retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood for 2025 (Euromonitor data, GFI report of April 2026). That was +8% nominal, about +4% real and +3% in volume.

(c) With no change, 2026 would be about $6.6B, assuming the 2025 baseline is not restated.

(d) Recent nominal growth has been 4-8% a year. Continuing that gives about $6.85-7.1B. The drivers point slightly up:
- Europe is growing, with German volumes reportedly +17% in early 2026.
- Beyond Meat's international retail is up 16.5%.
- The 2026 EUR/USD average is likely somewhat above 2025's, which gives a modest currency tailwind.
- Against that, US sales keep falling by about 10%.

(e) Growth from one year to the next is about ±5%. Euromonitor restatements of earlier years have also been about ±5%: 2023 was revised from $6.4B to about $5.9B. Together, these make a plausible range of roughly ±10% around the trend.

(f) I found no markets or expert forecasts on this exact figure. Commercial market-research numbers use a different scope and are not comparable.

(g) Scenarios:
- **Low:** Euromonitor revises its history down sharply, as it did in 2025, and the European recovery fades. Combined with continued US declines and a weaker euro in late 2026, that could give about $5.8-6.0B.
- **High:** Euromonitor revises upward and European and Asian growth accelerate. Add a favourable currency average and the figure could reach $7.8-8.2B.

My median is about $6.9B, with a downside skew from the risk of restatement.

(c) If nothing changed, the 2026 figure would be about $6.6B.

(d) If the trend continued, nominal growth of 4-8% would give roughly $6.85-7.1B. Several factors push in different directions:
- Europe is growing. German volumes were reportedly up 17% in early 2026, though this is secondhand.
- US sales are still falling by about 10%.

My central estimate is about $7.0B.

A revision to the 2025 baseline could therefore shift the 2026 figure as much as a full year of growth.

(f) There are no markets or expert forecasts on this exact series. Commercial market-research figures use different scopes and are not comparable.

(g) Low scenario: Euromonitor restates its methodology and revises 2025 down to about $6.0B. Combined with a weaker dollar-adjusted Asia, stalling European growth and a steep US decline, 2026 could come in near $5.6-5.8B.
High scenario: strong European momentum, a favorable currency effect and an upward restatement that adds markets or channels could push the figure to about $8B or more.

(e) **Historical variation:** Year-on-year changes in the first-published figures have ranged from about -5% (6.4 to 6.1, including the revision) to +8%. Restatements between editions have been about ±5%. The combined one-year uncertainty is roughly ±8-10%.
